findings.title: SSH is open to the internet on both droplets (admin_ip_ranges default 0.0.0.0/0 and CI never overrides it)
evidence: infra/terraform/digitalocean/variables.tf:76-91 — admin_ip_ranges is REQUIRED (no default) and validates length > 0; the comment states SSH can never be silently fail-open
infra/terraform/digitalocean/firewall.tf:20-24 — the DO firewall SSH rule uses source_addresses = var.admin_ip_ranges (no hardcoded 0.0.0.0/0)
infra/terraform/digitalocean/cloud-init.yml:23-26 — UFW renders one `ufw allow from ${cidr} to any port 22` per admin_ip_ranges entry
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:99-110 — pre-plan step fails when secrets.ADMIN_IP_RANGES is empty or contains 0.0.0.0/0 / ::/0
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:74-76 — ADMIN_IP_RANGES is read from secrets and written into the generated tfvars
findings.impact: A world-open SSH allowlist can no longer be applied by CI or by a plain terraform apply; the previous P1 (SSH exposed on both droplets) is closed in code.
findings.recommendation: Keep the fail-closed variable and guard. Operator action remains: set ADMIN_IP_RANGES (office/VPN CIDRs) in the dev and prod environments before the next apply; re-verify the live DO firewall + UFW after apply.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: variables.tf has no default + validation; terraform-do.yml rejects empty/world-open CIDRs before plan; cloud-init mirrors the list into UFW. Residual is operator-gated (set the secret), not code.

findings.title: Terraform state-locking fix is incompatible with the pinned Terraform version (use_lockfile requires >= 1.10, workflows pin 1.9)
evidence: infra/terraform/digitalocean/providers.tf:2-4 — required_version = ">= 1.15" with a comment tying it to use_lockfile
infra/terraform/digitalocean/providers.tf:16-18 — backend s3 uses use_lockfile = true
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:52,215,255 — hashicorp/setup-terraform terraform_version: 1.15.9 in plan and both apply jobs
scripts/install-terraform.ps1:5 — downloads terraform 1.15.9 for Windows operators
findings.impact: S3-native state locking is actually supported by the pinned toolchain, so concurrent applies can no longer corrupt state on a version mismatch.
findings.recommendation: No change; keep the version pin and required_version in sync if the toolchain is bumped.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: required_version >= 1.15 + workflow/script pin 1.15.9 both present and mutually consistent.

findings.title: Prometheus alert rules have no delivery path (no Alertmanager)
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:244-307 — alertmanager service (prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1 digest-pinned, envsubst-style awk render, healthcheck on /-/healthy)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:226-228 — prometheus depends_on alertmanager: service_healthy
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.yml:14-17 — alerting.alertmanagers target alertmanager:9093
infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml:86-100,147-152 — Watchdog route to the external watchdog receiver
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:739-747 — prod deploy fails when ALERTMANAGER_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK_URL is empty (IR-P0-003 fail-closed)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:801-805 — alertmanager.tmpl.yml is copied to /opt/mct-portal before compose up
findings.impact: Firing alerts now have a delivery path (ntfy/Slack webhook receivers) plus an off-box dead-man's switch; the rule-evaluation-only gap is closed.
findings.recommendation: No code change. Operator: provision ALERTMANAGER_CRITICAL_WEBHOOK_URL + ALERTMANAGER_WEBHOOK_USER/PASS (ntfy relay) and confirm a test alert lands in the portal topic.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: Alertmanager service + routing template + deploy-time fail-closed guard all present.

findings.title: Dev droplet capacity is under-provisioned and the CI value drifts from dev.tfvars.example
evidence: .github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:77-81 — DROPLET_SIZE resolves to s-2vcpu-2gb (prod) / s-1vcpu-2gb (dev), with a comment naming INFRA-P2-004 and the live dev droplet
infra/terraform/digitalocean/env/dev.tfvars.example:6-9 — droplet_size = "s-1vcpu-2gb" with the same rationale
infra/terraform/digitalocean/variables.tf:24-28 — droplet_size default s-2vcpu-2gb (prod default)
findings.impact: The CI apply and the documented dev tfvars now agree, so a dev apply will not silently recreate/shrink the droplet.
findings.recommendation: No change; if the compose stack grows, revisit the 2GB floor in both places together.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: CI dev size and dev.tfvars.example both s-1vcpu-2gb (PR #51 lineage).

findings.title: Operations documentation contradicts the current pipeline and configuration
evidence: docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:54 — claims deploy concurrency uses cancel-in-progress: true; deploy-do.yml:43 sets cancel-in-progress: false
docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:144 — claims terraform-do is "Triggered on push to main/develop"; terraform-do.yml:3-16 is manual-dispatch only (plus a dormant weekly schedule)
docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:137 — lists firewall ports 22/80/443/2376; firewall.tf:20-48 has no 2376 rule and cloud-init.yml:29-30 explicitly says "do NOT open 2376"
docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:48 — says Migrations are required for "All deploys"; deploy-do.yml:531-535 gates migrate-gate to prod only
docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:38 — documents API health "(200/526)" and web "(non-000)"; deploy-do.yml:893-934 requires API 200, web 200/301/302/307 and a fatal worker probe
docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:58 — says old images are pruned via `docker image prune -af`; deploy-do.yml:861-862 uses `docker rmi -f` on mct-* plus `docker image prune -f`
docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:92 — documents Redis health as `redis-cli -a <password>`; compose:56-61 authenticates via REDISCLI_AUTH to keep the password off argv

docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:219-220 — documents Terraform state at bucket mct-portal-tfstate-<env> key terraform/do/terraform.tfstate; env/backend.prod.hcl:4-5 is portal-terraform-state-production + digitalocean/prod/terraform.tfstate
infra/digitalocean/README.md:9-16 — service table lists 6 services and omits alertmanager; supporting-file list (45-51) omits alertmanager.tmpl.yml and metrics-token
docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:78 — calls METRICS_TOKEN an optional bearer gate; it is now required for the Prometheus scrape, and the matrix has no ALERTMANAGER_* or NTFY_ALERTS_* rows
docs/CI.md:23-25 and docs/RELEASING.md:130-131 — describe backup/restore failure notification as Slack; db-backup.yml:48-66 now posts to ntfy (NTFY_ALERTS_*) with Slack as fallback
findings.impact: Operators following the handbook/runbook can take wrong actions during an incident (wrong concurrency expectation, wrong firewall assumption, wrong rollback/state paths, wrong health semantics) and cannot find the alerting secrets they must provision.
findings.recommendation: Do one docs-sync PR: fix FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md (concurrency, terraform trigger, firewall ports, migration gating, health checks, prune, redis health), fix ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md §4 state paths and push-to-apply step, add alertmanager + metrics-token to infra/digitalocean/README.md, and add ALERTMANAGER_*/NTFY_ALERTS_*/METRICS_TOKEN rows to GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md. Add a doc guard (grep-based check) for the handful of load-bearing facts (concurrency value, terraform trigger, 2376 absence).
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: some docs were updated (CI.md, FINAL_OPERATOR_MAP.md, README.md, RELEASING.md) but the operations handbook, rollback §4, infra README and secrets matrix still contradict the code. Previously open (carried from 20261002); this run re-checked every cited line.

findings.title: Integration/security env vars referenced by the app schema are not delivered by the deploy pipeline
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:578-637 — every app-schema integration/security secret is forwarded to the setup step as an env var
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:647 — envs list contains 50 names; a mechanical diff shows 46 printf-written vars + 4 control vars and no name mismatch
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:669-716 — all 46 vars are written to /opt/mct-portal/.env via printf (no shell re-expansion), chmod 600 at :717
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:718-727 — METRICS_TOKEN is written to /opt/mct-portal/metrics-token, chowned 65534:65534, mode 400, matching the prom/prometheus container user (commit 00cb3da6)

apps/api/src/config/env.ts:19-74 and apps/worker/src/env.ts:5-43 — schema cross-check: every non-defaulted var in both schemas is present in the deploy envs list; only optional tunables (SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE, SENTRY_RELEASE, WORKER_CONCURRENCY, WORKER_TIMEOUT, SQS_QUEUE_URL, TASK_QUEUE_ENABLED) rely on code defaults
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:88,216,26-28 — METRICS_TOKEN is passed to the API and the token file is mounted read-only into Prometheus, with credentials_file wired in prometheus.yml:26-28
findings.impact: The original gap (schema vars never reaching the droplet) is closed for every required and integration/security variable, including the new alerting and metrics wiring.
findings.recommendation: No change. Optional follow-up: a small CI check that diffs the two Zod schemas against the deploy envs list so a future schema var cannot be added without delivery.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d with a mechanical comparison (50 envs vs 46 printf writes vs compose ${...} references): no drift. Correction to the prior note: NTFY_ALERTS_* are CI-only notifier secrets for db-backup/storage-backup/db-restore-test (db-backup.yml:48-66), not droplet .env vars; they are correctly absent from deploy-do.

findings.title: Redis container hardening was weakened and its password remains in process arguments
evidence: infra/digitalocean/redis-entrypoint.sh:13-21 — writes requirepass to a 0600 /tmp/redis.conf and execs redis-server with the file (password never on argv)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:37 — user: redis (the entrypoint replaces the official privilege-dropping one)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:56-61 — healthcheck authenticates via REDISCLI_AUTH env, not `-a <password>`
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:3-7,30 — cap_drop ALL + no-new-privileges; :44 REDIS_PASSWORD required with no fallback
findings.impact: The password is no longer readable via `ps`/docker inspect argv, and the container keeps the hardened capability profile.
findings.recommendation: No change; keep the entrypoint and the REDISCLI_AUTH healthcheck together if Redis is upgraded.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: password-file entrypoint + user:redis + REDISCLI_AUTH healthcheck all present.

findings.title: `env/prod.tfvars` is tracked despite an ignore rule that names it
evidence: .gitignore:57 — `**/env/*.tfvars` ignore rule
git ls-files output — only infra/terraform/digitalocean/env/dev.tfvars.example and env/prod.tfvars.example are tracked; no real tfvars file
git check-ignore -v — confirms infra/terraform/digitalocean/env/dev.tfvars is ignored
findings.impact: Real tfvars (secrets) under env/ can no longer be committed accidentally; the previous tracking mistake is gone.
findings.recommendation: No change to the env/ rule; see the separate finding about the module-root tfvars path the CI workflow and one runbook use.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: only *.example files are tracked; the ignore rule matches the env/ paths.

findings.title: Restore test uses a different Postgres major than the backup script and verifies only table counts
evidence: scripts/backup-database.sh:45-50 — docker fallback dumps with `postgres:15` when no local pg_dump exists (CI runners have pg_dump installed, so this path is off-CI)
.github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:110-116 — restores into postgres:16-alpine

.github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:135-232 — verification is no longer table-count-only: it asserts public tables, migrations, critical-table rows, newest audit_logs age (RPO canary), tenant-scoping columns and RLS-enabled counts, failing with ::error
.github/restore-test-baseline.env:1-27 — documented floors (RESTORE_MIN_TABLES=120, RESTORE_MAX_DATA_AGE_DAYS=2, RESTORE_MAX_TABLES_WITHOUT_RLS=0)
findings.impact: The deep-verification half of the finding is fixed (a truncated/stale/policy-stripped dump now fails). The residual version skew only affects the non-CI docker fallback path, which could dump with a client major different from the server being restored.
findings.recommendation: Pin both sides to the same major (e.g. postgres:16 in scripts/backup-database.sh:48, or make the version a single variable), and state the Supabase server major in the runbook so the client is chosen deliberately.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: verification is now deep (IR-P1-004 fix), but the docker fallback still pins postgres:15 vs postgres:16-alpine in the restore test.

findings.title: `docs/RTO_RPO.md` claims Redis AOF persistence that compose does not enable
evidence: docs/RTO_RPO.md:12 — Redis row: "AOF persistence; recreated from DB on loss"
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:27-61 — the redis service sets no command/appendonly config and mounts redis-data; the only redis.conf written is redis-entrypoint.sh:17-21 (`requirepass` only)
redis:7-alpine defaults — RDB snapshotting only; no appendonly
findings.impact: The documented Redis RPO (24h) is not backed by AOF; queue state on restart depends on RDB snapshots, and in-flight BullMQ jobs can be lost without the documented mitigation being real.
findings.recommendation: Either enable AOF (`--appendonly yes` with the named volume, verify memory/disk impact on the 1-vCPU dev droplet) or correct RTO_RPO.md to state RDB-snapshot-only and that in-flight queue work is re-driven by producers/retries. Add a comment in compose recording the decision.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: no appendonly anywhere in the stack; RTO_RPO.md:12 unchanged. Previously open (carried from 20261002).

findings.title: `infra/terraform/README.md` references an `aws/` directory that does not exist
evidence: infra/terraform/README.md:3-6 — now states the AWS root "was removed after the migration to DigitalOcean" and documents only digitalocean/
git log — commit c5b579be "chore(infra): ... drop dead aws/ reference"
findings.impact: The README no longer sends operators looking for a non-existent directory.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: README explicitly records the AWS removal and the digitalocean-only layout.

findings.title: Terraform is manual-dispatch only, so the "push to trigger apply" rollback runbook step is a no-op
evidence: docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:199-203 — "Push to trigger terraform-do workflow" / "will run a plan on the PR/push and apply automatically (dev) or require prod-approval (main)"
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:3-16 — on: schedule + workflow_dispatch only; a comment records the 2026-09-29 decision
docs/CI.md:98-104 and docs/FINAL_OPERATOR_MAP.md:34 — already document manual-dispatch only, so the runbook is the outlier
findings.impact: An operator following §4 during an infrastructure rollback pushes a revert and believes an apply was triggered; nothing runs, and the rollback silently does not happen.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md §4 to "merge the revert, then dispatch terraform-do with apply=true (prod requires prod-approval)" and delete the push-to-trigger sentence. Optionally cross-link docs/CI.md.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: terraform-do.yml has no push/PR triggers, ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:199-203 still instructs pushing to trigger. Previously open (carried from 20261002).

findings.title: Manual rollback script cannot authenticate to GHCR and defaults to the wrong image prefix
evidence: scripts/rollback.sh:25 — GHCR_PREFIX default is `ghcr.io/mainecybertech/mainecybertech-portal`; the pipeline and compose use `ghcr.io/mainecybertech/mainecybertech` (deploy-do.yml:97 computes it from github.repository; infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:69)

scripts/rollback.sh:42-51 — the remote heredoc references $GHCR_TOKEN/$GHCR_USER but the ssh command forwards neither (no SendEnv; the vars are not passed as arguments), so the login line fails (unbound variable under set -u, swallowed by `|| true`) and no registry login happens
scripts/rollback.sh:63-67 — API health check treats ANY non-000 HTTP code as success (a 500 passes)
scripts/rollback.sh:70-72 — worker health is explicitly non-fatal ("skipped (non-fatal)"), contradicting the pipeline's fatal worker gate (deploy-do.yml:905-922)
scripts/rollback.sh:42,70 — StrictHostKeyChecking=no on both ssh invocations, while the pipeline verifies a pinned host key (deploy-do.yml:883-891)
findings.impact: The documented manual rollback tool (scripts/README.md:37) fails or reports success incorrectly during an incident: the wrong prefix means it pulls nothing unless GHCR_PREFIX is overridden, and even then the private-registry login cannot succeed. Weak health checks can declare a broken rollback complete.
findings.recommendation: Fix the script in one PR: default GHCR_PREFIX to `ghcr.io/mainecybertech/mainecybertech` (or read it from the compose/.env), pass GHCR_TOKEN/GHCR_USER as ssh arguments (or require `docker login` on the droplet first), make worker health fatal, require 200/301/302/307 for the API/web checks, and use StrictHostKeyChecking=yes with a pinned host key (or explicitly document it as the last-resort path). Add a CI shellcheck/lint pass and keep it in parity with deploy-do's health gate.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; found while auditing the rollback path (domain scope: deploy scripts, rollback). Not run against the droplet.

findings.title: Deploy health gate ignores the monitoring and reverse-proxy containers
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:835-858 — the container-health gate inspects only mct-portal-api-1, mct-portal-web-1 and mct-portal-worker-1; alertmanager, prometheus, caddy and redis are never asserted

infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:244-307 — alertmanager renders alertmanager.tmpl.yml with an awk one-liner that exits non-zero if any placeholder survives (container restart-loops on failure); prometheus depends_on it (:226-228), so a broken alertmanager also removes Prometheus
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:207-237 — prometheus has no healthcheck at all
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:302-307 — alertmanager DOES define a healthcheck, so it could be asserted but is not
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:728-752 — the only alerting guard is the prod watchdog-URL emptiness check; nothing verifies the rendered config or the running container
findings.impact: A deploy can finish green while the alert delivery path (Alertmanager/Prometheus) is down, so rule-based alerts and the internal metrics pipeline are silently absent. In prod the external dead-man's switch eventually pages; in dev (no watchdog) the loss is silent, and the deploy reports success.
findings.recommendation: Extend the health gate to assert `container_health alertmanager` (and optionally prometheus/caddy), or add a post-up `docker compose ps` assertion that every service with a healthcheck is healthy, failing the deploy (and triggering the existing rollback) otherwise. Also consider a `promtool check config`-style pre-flight in the deploy or CI.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Related: CTR-P2-004 fixed the worker half of the gate; this is the observability half.

findings.title: infra/digitalocean/.env.example omits the alerting and internal-metrics variables the compose stack reads
evidence: infra/digitalocean/.env.example:1-71 — contains no METRICS_TOKEN, ALERTMANAGER_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK_URL, ALERTMANAGER_CRITICAL_WEBHOOK_URL, ALERTMANAGER_DEFAULT_WEBHOOK_URL, ALERTMANAGER_SLACK_API_URL, ALERTMANAGER_WEBHOOK_USER/PASS, MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED, JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET, JSM_WEBHOOK_SECRET or M365_CLIENT_STATE
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:88,216 — METRICS_TOKEN and the ./metrics-token mount are part of the API/Prometheus wiring
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:251-266 — alertmanager reads seven ALERTMANAGER_* variables, each defaulting to a no-op loopback URL when unset
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:89,91-92 — MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED, JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET and JSM_WEBHOOK_SECRET are read from .env
findings.impact: An operator provisioning the stack by hand from .env.example (the file the infra README calls the template) silently gets no metrics auth and a no-op alert delivery path, with no boot error. The CI deploy path is unaffected because it writes .env from secrets.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing keys to infra/digitalocean/.env.example with explanatory comments (especially that ALERTMANAGER_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK_URL must be an off-box URL and METRICS_TOKEN must match the API/Prometheus pair), and keep it in sync with compose. Optionally add a CI check that every ${VAR:?...} / ${VAR...} in the droplet compose appears in the example.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the app-level .env.example files (apps/api, apps/worker, apps/web) are current — this is the droplet template only.

findings.title: Terraform tfvars generated/referenced at the module root are not covered by the .gitignore rule
evidence: .gitignore:57 — the only tfvars rule is `**/env/*.tfvars`
git check-ignore -v infra/terraform/digitalocean/dev.tfvars — no match (not ignored); only env/dev.tfvars is ignored

.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:66-95 — the workflow writes $TF_ENV.tfvars into the module root (working-directory infra/terraform/digitalocean), containing DO/Cloudflare tokens and the SSH allowlist
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:209-211,230 — the runbook tells operators to run `terraform plan -var-file=dev.tfvars` in infra/terraform/digitalocean, the same unignored path
scripts/validate-terraform-env.sh:7-8,17 — the placeholder guard only scans env/*.tfvars, so it would not scan a module-root file either
findings.impact: An operator following the rollback runbook creates a secrets-bearing tfvars at a path git does not ignore; a routine `git add -A` could commit live DO and Cloudflare credentials. CI-generated files are ephemeral, so the exposure is the documented local workflow.
findings.recommendation: Widen the ignore to the whole module (e.g. `infra/terraform/**/*.tfvars` with `!*.example`) or change the workflow/runbook to always use env/<env>.tfvars. Extend validate-terraform-env.sh to scan both locations, and add a pre-commit/gitleaks rule for tfvars contents.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; complements INFRA-P3-008 (the env/ rule works, the module-root path is uncovered).

findings.title: Cloud-init UFW SSH allowlist is applied only at droplet creation, so narrowed allowlists leave stale host rules
evidence: infra/terraform/digitalocean/droplet.tf:11-20 — user_data (cloud-init) renders the UFW rules; lifecycle ignore_changes = [user_data] means an existing droplet is never re-rendered
infra/terraform/digitalocean/cloud-init.yml:23-26 — per-CIDR `ufw allow from ...` rules are additive at first boot
infra/terraform/digitalocean/firewall.tf:12-24 — the DO cloud firewall is the authoritative allowlist and does update on apply, so removal is enforced at the network edge
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth drift: after narrowing admin_ip_ranges, the droplet's UFW still allows the removed CIDRs. The DO firewall still blocks them, so the effective control holds, but the in-host layer no longer mirrors the documented "UFW mirrors this same allowlist" claim (firewall.tf:15).
findings.recommendation: Either manage UFW out-of-band (a documented `ufw --force reset` + re-add procedure, or an ansible/ssh step in the deploy) or soften the firewall.tf comment and record the create-time-only behavior in docs. A small terraform `null_resource`/remote-exec is not recommended on the deploy path; documentation plus a runbook step is the low-risk fix.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; code-only evidence, live droplet UFW not inspected (no authorization).

findings.title: METRICS_TOKEN has no fail-closed deploy guard; an empty token leaves the API scrape permanently down
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:739-747 — prod fail-closed guard exists only for ALERTMANAGER_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK_URL
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:722-727 — an empty METRICS_TOKEN still writes an empty /opt/mct-portal/metrics-token file
apps/api/src/config/env.ts:61-63 — METRICS_TOKEN is optional in the schema
apps/api/src/app.ts:154-171 — when no token is configured the API 404s every /metrics request
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.yml:20-32 — the mct-api scrape sends the credentials file as a bearer token; a 404 makes up==0
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:8-16 — MCTServiceDown fires on up==0 for mct-api/mct-worker for 2m
findings.impact: If METRICS_TOKEN is missing in an environment, the deploy stays green but the API scrape is permanently down: MCTServiceDown fires continuously (alert noise that can mask real outages) and the RLS/impersonation rules never evaluate because their metrics are absent. This is a configuration-drift footgun, not an exposure (the endpoint fails closed).
findings.recommendation: Treat METRICS_TOKEN like the watchdog in prod: fail the deploy when it is empty (or when the written token file is empty), and/or make the Prometheus api scrape conditional. Add a post-deploy assertion that the mct-api target is up.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the prod secret is reported set in the 20261011 reconciliation, so this is a structural guard gap, not a live outage claim.

findings.title: Prometheus alert-rule unit tests exist but are not run in CI
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.test.yml:1-8 — promtool unit tests with a header documenting the manual `docker run ... promtool test rules` commands; they exist because two earlier versions of MCTTenantScopeRegression could never fire
grep for promtool/rules.test across .github/ and package.json — no workflow or composite action invokes them (only deploy-do.yml copies prometheus.rules.yml to the droplet)
.github/workflows/validate.yml:1-110 — the deploy gate runs shell-exec-bit, branch-protection, unit, secret, lint, typecheck and prompt-provenance checks, but no Prometheus rule check
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:1-4 — rules are copied verbatim to the droplet by deploy-do.yml:800, so a syntactically valid but non-firing rule ships silently
findings.impact: The regression the test file was written to prevent (a rule that can never fire, or a syntax break) can re-enter through a PR with no CI signal; the only guard is someone remembering to run promtool manually.
findings.recommendation: Add a small CI job (or a step in validate.yml's audit job) that runs `promtool check rules` and `promtool test rules` against the pinned prom/prometheus:v3.5.1 image (same command documented in the test file header). It is fast and needs no credentials.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; OBS-P2-001's note records a manual promtool run, but no CI wiring exists.

report:
# Infrastructure, Deployment, and Environment Drift Audit

## Executive Summary

The infrastructure domain is in materially better shape than at the 20261004 baseline. The 12 INFRA rows from the previous register were re-verified at `8d299b8d`: **8 are verified-fixed**, 1 is partially-fixed, and 3 remain open (all documentation/configuration drift). The strongest work is in the deploy pipeline: the droplet `.env` is now written from 46 secrets with no shell re-expansion, the env-delivery gap (INFRA–P2-006) is closed for every non-defaulted schema variable, `METRICS_TOKEN` is delivered to both the API and the Prometheus scrape via a 0600/400 file owned by the container user (commits `8f8dbe42`, `ddbc389c`, `00cb3da6`), and the Alertmanager/ntfy dead-man's switch is fully wired with a prod fail-closed guard.

Remaining risks cluster in three places. **(1) Operator-facing truth drift:** the deployment handbook, rollback runbook §4, the infra README and the secrets matrix still describe the pre-remediation pipeline (concurrency, Terraform triggers, firewall port 2376, migration gating, health semantics, state bucket names, Slack-only alerting, optional METRICS_TOKEN). **(2) The manual rollback tool is broken:** `scripts/rollback.sh` defaults to a stale GHCR prefix and never forwards registry credentials, and its health checks are weaker than the pipeline's. **(3) Deploy confidence stops at api/web/worker:** a deploy can finish green while Alertmanager/Prometheus (the alert delivery path) is down, and an empty `METRICS_TOKEN` produces a permanently-failing API scrape with no deploy-time guard. Live Terraform-vs-droplet drift remains unverifiable from the repository; the weekly plan-only drift check is present but dormant (`TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED` unset) and the DO token is reportedly 401 (CI-domain rows own that).

Recommended next actions: fix `scripts/rollback.sh` (P2), extend the deploy health gate to the monitoring containers (P2), and do a single documentation-sync PR (P2/P3) covering every contradiction listed in the findings.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Droplet compose stack

- Evidence: `infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:1-344`.
- What it does: defines redis, api, worker, web, prometheus, alertmanager, caddy with shared `x-security` (cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges) and bounded json-file logging.
- How it appears to work: deploy copies the file to `/opt/mct-portal/` and runs `docker compose -p mct-portal up -d` with `IMAGE_TAG`/`GHCR_IMAGE_PREFIX`.
- Dependencies: `.env`, `redis-entrypoint.sh`, `prometheus.yml`, `prometheus.rules.yml`, `alertmanager.tmpl.yml`, `Caddyfile*`, `certs/`, `metrics-token` — all copied by `deploy-do.yml:789-805` (metrics-token written at `:722-727`).
- Current controls: `${VAR:?}` for SUPABASE_*/JWT_SECRET/REDIS_PASSWORD/IMAGE_TAG; read-only rootfs for api/worker/web/prometheus/alertmanager; tmpfs `/tmp`; healthchecks on redis/api/worker/alertmanager/caddy.
- Missing controls: no healthcheck on prometheus; the deploy gate does not assert alertmanager/prometheus/caddy.
- Risks: a broken alerting path can ship green (see finding).
- Recommended improvement: assert every healthchecked service in the deploy gate.
- Suggested tests: CI `docker compose config` render check with a fixture `.env`; a compose-level healthcheck assertion script.
- Suggested docs: add alertmanager/metrics-token to `infra/digitalocean/README.md`.

### Item: Terraform droplet/firewall/DNS

- Evidence: `variables.tf:76-92`, `firewall.tf:20-48`, `cloud-init.yml:19-30`, `droplet.tf:1-21`, `dns.tf:1-73`, `providers.tf:1-31`, `env/backend.*.hcl`, `.terraform.lock.hcl`.
